item.title: Himeji Castle: Japan's Finest Surviving Castle — Guide
item.description: Himeji Castle is the greatest surviving castle in Japan and one of the finest in the world: completed in its present form in 1609, it escaped the fires, sieges, demolition orders and wartime bombing that destroyed almost every other Japanese castle, and stands today entirely original. Its brilliant white plastered walls and layered gables earned it the nickname Shirasagi-jo, the White Heron Castle, and its defensive design — a spiralling maze of gates, walled lanes and dead ends climbing to the six-storey keep — is as impressive as its beauty.
